checks.invariant: kind()/_norm/_parts classify every name that a downstream consumer would treat as an instruction file, and every caller (policy.decide match.instruction_files, service.outbox badge, service.export_file audit flag, api.outbox_file download, _outbox.html) routes attacker names through it; and the download path is gated by clean_name.
checks.result: _norm applies NFKC+casefold (covers fullwidth/U+017F), strips an NTFS ':' stream suffix, and rstrip('. ') for trailing dot/space; _parts does str.strip() first, normalizes forward-slash '..' with posixpath.normpath, and splits backslash parts without resolving backslash '..' (the IF-1 F2 fix holds). kind() matches _NAMES on the last part, _DIRS on any earlier part, and .github/<instructions|prompts|chatmodes>/<more> with a correct bound. policy.decide only treats path tools and only when args['path'] or resolved_path has a kind. clean_name (_BAD_NAME=[\x00-\x1f\x7f/\\]) rejects C0/DEL and path separators on the export/download path; browser download sanitizers replace reserved characters (yielding a different name) and only remove trailing whitespace/dots, which kind already folds, so an exact browser rename to a canonical name is not reachable. 8.3 short names alias an already-existing long file and cannot be synthesized via write_file. Over-matching is conservative by design.

checks.invariant: Battery of residual-bypass inputs classify as intended: canonical names, prior fixes, default-ignorable/zero-width characters, 8.3 names, trailing non-whitespace chars, .github boundary conditions, and colon over-match.
checks.result: kind() matched all canonical names and all prior-fix variants; it returned None for zero-width/default-ignorable variants (claude\u200b.md, \ufeffclaude.md, soft hyphen), which a downstream agent reading by exact name would also not treat as CLAUDE.md. Trailing tab/newline/ideographic space were stripped; trailing DEL/NUL were not but are blocked by clean_name at download. .github/instructions (no trailing part) returns None while .github/instructions/a.md matches. foo:CLAUDE.md -> 'foo'. CLAUDE~1.MD -> None.

checks.invariant: Turkish dotted capital I (U+0130) casefold expansion vs OS case-insensitive fold, and clean_name behaviour on the download name for such names and C1 control chars.
checks.result: kind('gemİni.md') == None because casefold() expands U+0130 to 'i'+U+0307 giving 'gemi̇ni.md' != 'gemini.md'. clean_name accepts 'gemİni.md' and 'CLAUDE.md\x81' (C1) and rejects 'CLAUDE.md\x7f'. Whether a case-insensitive volume equates the U+0130 name to the canonical name is not locally observable.

candidates.title: kind() casefold expands U+0130 and may miss an instruction name that a case-insensitive filesystem treats as canonical
candidates.description: _norm normalizes a name with unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', name).casefold(). Python's full casefold expands LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE (U+0130) to 'i' followed by U+0307 COMBINING DOT ABOVE, so kind('gemİni.md') returns None. clean_name accepts the name on the outbox download path, outbox()/_outbox.html show no instruction-file badge, and the write never hit the instruction-file approval rule. If a recipient on a case-insensitive volume equates 'gemİni.md' to 'gemini.md', the human's other coding agent auto-reads attacker content as an instruction file, the same boundary the a0a186c fullwidth/U+017F fix was meant to close. NTFS $UpCase does not equate U+0130 with ASCII 'i', so Windows recipients are not affected; the open question is macOS and other case-insensitive volumes.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: _norm relies on Python's full casefold, which maps U+0130 to an ASCII letter plus a combining mark, diverging from an OS case-insensitive fold that may map U+0130 to plain 'i'; kind() therefore misclassifies a name a case-insensitive filesystem might resolve to a canonical instruction name.

trace.description: A prompt-injected agent calls write_file with path 'outbox/gemİni.md'; kind() of path and resolved_path is None, so the instruction-file-write-needs-approval rule does not fire.
casefold() expands U+0130 to 'i'+U+0307, so _norm('gemİni.md')='gemi̇ni.md' and kind() returns None.
outbox() calls IF.kind(f['name']) which returns None, so no instruction_file flag or badge is shown.
The human downloads the file (clean_name accepts the name); on a volume that folds U+0130 to 'i' the saved name could resolve to 'gemini.md'.

evidence.description: n = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', name).casefold(); observed locally (h2.out): kind('gemİni.md')=None while kind('gemini.md')='Gemini CLI'.
clean_name accepts 'gemİni.md' (observed h2.out), so the name is downloadable from the outbox.
decide() keys the instruction-file approval solely on kind(path)/kind(resolved_path).

blockers: Whether a real case-insensitive filesystem (APFS/HFS+ on macOS) equates a filename containing U+0130 with the ASCII-'i' canonical name is OS behaviour not observable in the Linux-only, offline audit sandbox.
Whether a recipient coding agent on such a volume loads the aliased name requires that agent and OS at runtime.
NTFS $UpCase is documented not to equate U+0130 with ASCII 'i', so the Windows recipient path is excluded.

validation_plan.local: Already run in the approved sandbox (h2.out). Extend by enumerating every character whose casefold expands to an ASCII letter used in _NAMES/_DIRS plus a combining or invisible code point.
validation_plan.deployment: On an owner-controlled macOS machine with an APFS case-insensitive volume, create a file literally named 'gemİni.md' and check whether `stat gemini.md` resolves to it and whether `ls` shows one or two files. If it aliases, fold names for classification with a mapping that does not introduce combining marks (for example NFKD, drop Mn, then casefold, or special-case U+0130).

hardening: clean_name (_BAD_NAME) rejects C0 and DEL but not C1 controls (U+0080-U+009F); extending _BAD_NAME to C1 would remove an uncertain download-name surface.
8.3 short names (CLAUDE~1.MD) are not classified by kind(); this cannot synthesize a canonical instruction file via write_file, so it is not a write-path bypass.
Over-matching is conservative by design (agent.md, anything under .roo/ or .continue/ goes to approval); note to operators to avoid approval fatigue.
Default-ignorable characters are preserved by NFKC and cause kind()=None, but a downstream agent reading by exact name would also not treat the name as canonical, so this is symmetric.
